rationale: Interpretation of the extended trim execution and correction of the trim knowledge entry. CheckRun 240d4355d55e4c7a91b5e0a01a0cc407 (exit 0, cases A-D passed) evaluated all four comparisons completely: the control {1,2,3} `holds` (trim(None) moved the compacted index 0 -> 1) while {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} (leader 2, id 1 absent) and the two-node {1,3} are each `violated` with valid witnesses (indices 3, 5, 7), every one of them reporting `trim_none_result` = ok with the compacted index unchanged and `trim_explicit_result` = not_all_decided:0. The trigger statement in the previous knowledge entry said the generalisation to other gapped id sets was derived from the sizing code and not executed; that premise has now changed, so I correct that entry under its existing id with the measured conditions and point it at the affected use. No new execution is needed this turn for that correction.

knowledge.changed_premise: The conditions no longer rest on a source-derived generalisation: the trigger was executed for two further id sets ({2,3,4} with a different leader and id 1 absent, and the two-node {1,3}) in addition to {1,2,5}, and all three keep the compacted index at 0 with trim(None) reporting ok and the documented explicit retry returning NotAllDecided(0). The statement, sources and scope are otherwise unchanged; only the conditions and the cited execution were updated.
knowledge.statement: With a configuration whose largest node id exceeds the number of nodes, the leader cannot advance the compacted index through `trim`. `LeaderState::with` allocates `accepted_indexes` for every id up to the largest one, phantom slots (ids that are not in the configuration) are never written, and `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` minimises over that whole vector, so the reduced value is 0 no matter how far the real servers have decided. `SequencePaxos::trim` therefore computes a trim index of 0 for `trim(None)`, `InternalStorage::try_trim(0)` finds nothing to compact and the call returns `Ok(())` while `get_compacted_idx()` is unchanged; `trim(Some(k))` for any k >= 1 fails the guard `idx <= min_all_accepted_idx` and returns `CompactionErr::NotAllDecided(0)`, so the documented repair step ('users can retry with omni_paxos.trim(Some(idx)) which will then succeed') cannot succeed. Measured on real instances with one entry decided by every configured server: {1,2,3} compacted 0 -> 1, while {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} (leader 2, id 1 absent) and the two-node {1,3} each stayed at 0 with `trim_none_result` = ok and `trim_explicit_result` = not_all_decided:0.
knowledge.conditions: Core crate with MemoryStorage, in-process lossless delivery, batch_size 1, majority quorum, one decided entry, leader = first id of each set. The measured trigger is any id set whose largest id exceeds the node count, equivalently any set leaving a phantom slot below the maximum: {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and {1,3} were executed; sets that are contiguous 1..=n (the control) are unaffected. Snapshot-based compaction is not affected by the reduced value (`try_snapshot` uses the decided index) and remains available as a workaround; decision counting is not affected either, because `is_chosen` only counts slots whose accepted index reaches the candidate index and phantom slots hold 0.

investigations.discriminator: Settled and measured for four id sets. Untested variants of the same cause, which would not change the account: a cluster where the ids are contiguous but start above 1 at a larger size, and trimming after a snapshot has already compacted part of the log.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, now carried by a four-case comparison chain. `LeaderState::with` allocates one accepted-index slot per id up to the largest id in the configuration and `LeaderState::get_min_all_accepted_idx` reduces over that whole vector, so any id set with a phantom slot below the maximum pins the reduced value at 0 however far the real servers have decided; `SequencePaxos::trim` compares the caller's index against that reduced value before asking `InternalStorage::try_trim` to compact, and `try_trim(0)` finds nothing to do while still returning Ok. The retained execution evaluates the declared predicate for four id sets with the same state (every configured server decided the same entry, decided index 1, compacted index 0): the contiguous control {1,2,3} `holds` (trim(None) advanced the compacted index to 1), and {1,2,5}, {2,3,4} and {1,3} are each `violated` with valid witnesses - in all three, trim(None) reported ok with the compacted index still 0 and the documented explicit retry returned `NotAllDecided(0)`, because the guard requires an index at or below the reduced value of 0. Two consequences follow for configurations the target's own validation accepts (only more than one node, a non-zero configuration id, valid quorums and that the node set contains this server's pid): the trim API silently reports success while making no progress, and the only remaining compaction path is snapshotting, so the documented 'highest trimmable index' semantics and the documented retry step both fail. The measured trigger is a largest id above the node count - covering sparse sets, sets that omit low ids, and small clusters with high ids - not the specific {1,2,5} shape probed first. Scope is progress/availability of trimming, not safety: phantom slots hold 0 and `is_chosen` counts only slots whose accepted index reaches the candidate index, so decision formation is unaffected, and `try_snapshot` uses the decided index rather than the reduced value.
counterevidence: Trimming is optional compaction: the cluster keeps making progress and the log stays correct, so the defect costs unbounded log growth and a misleading success return rather than lost work.
`try_snapshot` does not consult the reduced value, so a caller that snapshots (with or without `local_only`) can compact under the same configuration; the defect is confined to the trim path.

The probe used MemoryStorage and a lossless in-process transport, so nothing here speaks to a storage backend that rejects the no-op trim or to timing-sensitive behaviour, although the reduced value is computed in the core and does not depend on storage.

The control's explicit retry returned ok without further compaction because the preceding trim(None) had already compacted that index, so the control shows only that trim(None) compacts and that a later explicit call at the same index is accepted.
limitations: One entry decided, batch_size 1, majority quorum, at most four nodes; larger clusters or longer logs are unmeasured, though the reduced value depends on neither (other than through the id range).
No snapshot or snapshot-then-trim case was run, so the claim that snapshotting remains available is source-derived from `try_snapshot`/`InternalStorage` rather than measured.
The two-node {1,3} case exercises the same reduced value with a different majority rule; no flexible-quorum configuration was tried.
